summary: Backend-only security re-audit after the Telegram webhook removal. Verified POST /api/chat/telegram/webhook is fully unreachable (404 for POST and all other verbs, absent from /api/openapi.json, TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET gone from backend/.env, no telegram_subscribers side effect in MongoDB). Re-ran the full security suite: 414/414 PASS (test_security_full_audit.py 389 + test_security_reverify_extra.py included, test_security_bruteforce.py 2, test_security_auth_remediation.py 23). Also ran test_chat_and_per_employee_tasks.py (21/21 PASS) to confirm chat send-message, conversations, unread and /api/chat/image routing/auth were not broken by the removal. No new vulnerabilities, no regressions: RBAC on all admin endpoints rejects no-auth/employee/forged JWT, IDOR/BOLA blocked on contracts + employee documents + chat + my-contract, NoSQL injection on /api/applications/login returns 422, removed backdoors (/api/status, /api/admin/init-admin, /api/employee/init-employee) still 404/405, brute-force lockout (5x401 then 429) works on a throwaway email, no password_hash/app_password leakage, chat image path traversal blocked, public test-session tokens high-entropy with correct lifecycle. Cleanup script executed after the runs.
critical_code_review_comments: Informational (no action required for security): db.telegram_subscribers is now read-only - send_telegram_notification() still queries it but nothing writes to it since /start//stop registration was removed, so admin Telegram notifications will only fire for chat_ids already stored. If Telegram notifications are still a product requirement, subscribers must be seeded/managed by an authenticated admin route; otherwise the collection and send_telegram_notification() can be dropped.
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is still present in backend/.env although the only consumer is the outbound notification path - keep it only if the notification feature stays.
